summary: Describes how SNMP messages are processed and sent to the proper message processing models, and how requests are passed to SNMP applications. It also describes the SNMPv3 message processing model. It was replaced by RFC 2272.

eli5.summary: It is the mail room of a network manager. It sorts incoming messages and sends each to the right department.

questions: how does snmp message dispatching work
what is the snmpv3 message processing model
how does snmp route messages to applications
subtitle: The routing system inside SNMP engines that handles multiple protocol versions.

tldr.problem: SNMP engines need to handle multiple versions of SNMP (v1, v2, v3) and route messages to the correct version-specific handlers, security processors, and applications.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC defines an SNMP engine architecture with a Dispatcher that receives messages, determines the SNMP version, routes them to the appropriate Message Processing Model for that version, coordinates security processing, and then routes the PDU to the correct application.
tldr.outcome: SNMP engines can support multiple SNMP versions simultaneously, with extensible Message Processing Models for future versions. The RFC defines the SNMPv3 message format and processing procedures.

today: RFC 2262 is a Proposed Standard and was obsoleted by RFC 2272 in 1998, just a few months later. However, the core concepts of message dispatching and processing remain central to SNMP engines today. Modern SNMP implementations still use the dispatcher architecture described here to handle multiple SNMP versions simultaneously.

sections.title: Architecture and Overview
sections.content:
An SNMP engine consists of four main subsystems: a Dispatcher, a Message Processing Subsystem, a Security Subsystem, and an Access Control Subsystem. This RFC focuses on the first two, which work together to handle incoming and outgoing SNMP messages in a version-independent way.

The Dispatcher is the central hub. When an application wants to send an SNMP message, it provides the message to the Dispatcher along with information about which SNMP version to use, which security model to apply, and where to send it. When a message arrives from the network, the Dispatcher determines which version it is, passes it to the appropriate Message Processing Model to decode it, works with the Security Subsystem to verify security, and then routes the resulting PDU to the correct application.

Each Message Processing Model handles one SNMP version (v1, v2c, v3, or others). A message processing model knows how to parse that version's message format, extract the PDU, and handle any version-specific processing. The Dispatcher can contain multiple Message Processing Models at the same time, allowing an SNMP engine to support multiple SNMP versions simultaneously.
sections.eli5: The Dispatcher is the mail room. It takes outgoing letters from different offices, makes sure they are addressed correctly, and sends them. It also receives incoming letters, figures out which format they are in, opens them safely, and delivers them to the right office.

sections.title: Sending SNMP Messages
sections.content:
When an application wants to send an SNMP message, it calls the Dispatcher with an abstract service primitive that includes the destination address, the desired SNMP version (messageProcessingModel), the security model and level to apply, the context engine ID and context name, the PDU to send, and whether a response is expected.

The Dispatcher assigns a unique sendPduHandle to track this message through the system. It then delegates to the appropriate Message Processing Model to prepare the outgoing message. The Message Processing Model takes the PDU and the version-specific parameters, coordinates with the Security Subsystem to apply encryption or authentication as needed, and constructs the final SNMP message in the correct format for that version.

Once the message is prepared, the Dispatcher sends it to the specified address via the specified transport (typically UDP). For responses, a similar procedure is followed, except the application provides a stateReference that points back to the original request, and a maximum size for the response message.
sections.eli5: Sending a message: the office tells the mail room what to send and where. The mail room picks the right format, seals it securely if needed, and sends it out.

sections.title: Receiving and Dispatching Messages
sections.content:
When an SNMP message arrives from the network, the Dispatcher increments counters and determines the SNMP version from the message itself. It then passes the message to the appropriate Message Processing Model for that version. The Message Processing Model decodes the version-specific format, extracts the PDU, and extracts key data elements such as the contextEngineID, contextName, security parameters, and other metadata.

The Dispatcher coordinates with the Security Subsystem to process security: authentication and decryption are performed as needed based on the security model specified in the message. If security processing fails or the message is malformed, it is discarded.

If processing succeeds, the Dispatcher uses the pduType (the type of SNMP operation, such as GetRequest, SetRequest, or Trap) and the contextEngineID to determine which application should receive the PDU. The PDU is then dispatched to that application with the version information and security context. The application can then process the request or notification.
sections.eli5: Receiving a message: the mail room opens each letter, reads the address and security seal, and delivers it to the right office with all the important information.

sections.title: SNMPv3 Message Format
sections.content:
This RFC defines the format of SNMPv3 messages, which the SNMPv3 Message Processing Model uses. An SNMPv3 message consists of a message version field, a message ID for correlation with responses, a maximum message size the receiver can handle, and message flags that indicate whether authentication and encryption are being used.

The message also contains a security model identifier (indicating which security model is in use, such as user-based security for v3) and version-specific security parameters. The PDU is carried inside a scoped PDU that is wrapped with a context engine ID and context name. The context identifies which entity's management information is being accessed and in which context.

When encryption is used, the scoped PDU is encrypted. When authentication is used, a message authentication code (MAC) is computed over the message and included. The message can be sent with authentication, encryption, both, or neither, controlled by the flags.
sections.eli5: An SNMPv3 message is like a sealed envelope: it says who it is from, where it is going, which security to apply, and what you should do with it.

sections.title: Message Processing Models and Registration
sections.content:
The Message Processing Subsystem is designed to be extensible. Different Message Processing Models can be added to support different SNMP versions or variants. The SNMPv3 Message Processing Model is described in this RFC, but models for SNMPv1 and SNMPv2c could be added in the future if needed.

Applications register with the Dispatcher to handle specific combinations of pduType (e.g., GetRequest) and contextEngineID. When a PDU arrives for a pduType and contextEngineID pair, the Dispatcher routes it to the registered application.

The dispatcher also maintains statistics about SNMP engine behavior in managed objects (MIB variables), allowing remote management stations to monitor the health and activity of the SNMP engine itself. This includes counters for messages received, messages sent, errors, and other operational metrics.
sections.eli5: Different offices can register to handle different types of incoming messages. The mail room keeps track of how many messages of each type arrive and how many go out.
